content: Dr. Jeannie Yang, MD, presented an overview of neuroblastoma at the University of Wisconsin Department of Surgery Grand Rounds in 2007. Neuroblastic tumors are classified into seven subtypes based on the degree of neuroblastic maturation and the proportion of background Schwannian stroma. Below are detailed descriptions of three subtypes: 1. Undifferentiated Neuroblastoma: This subtype is composed entirely of neuroblasts without any evidence of ganglion cell maturation. Immunohistochemical analysis is often necessary to confirm the neuroblastic lineage of the tumor. The background Schwannian stroma is classified as poor, meaning it constitutes less than 50% of the stroma, and in some cases, it may be completely absent. 2. Poorly Differentiated Neuroblastoma: The tumor is predominantly composed of neuroblasts, with at least one identifiable focus of neuropil. Similar to the undifferentiated subtype, the Schwannian stroma is poor, comprising less than 50% of the background stroma, and it may also be absent. 3. Differentiating Neuroblastoma: This subtype is primarily composed of neuroblasts, but more than 5% of the cells show evidence of maturing or mature ganglion cell differentiation. At least one focus of neuropil is present. The Schwannian stroma remains poor, with less than 50% of the background stroma being Schwannian, and it may be absent in some cases.
